newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LDP says to discuss extra budget in Jan - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Japan LDP says to discuss extra budget in Jan - Jiji.

text.p: Japan will deal with the issue of whether to draw up a stimulative budget at the beginning of the regular parliament session in January, a senior coalition party official was quoted as saying by Japan's Jiji news agency.

Taku Yamazaki, a senior member of the Liberal Democratic Party, told reporters a schedule for discussing an extra budget for this fiscal year ending in March was decided in principle after talks among LDP members and the Finance Ministry, Jiji said.

Media reports earlier this month said Yamazaki had called for a supplementary budget worth about five trillion yen to be considered at a special parliamentary session after the general elections, which were held on October 20.
The reports quoted Yamazaki as saying in an election campaign speech that the extra budget must contain funds to finance 3.5 trillion yen worth of public works projects.
Jiji quoted Yamazaki as saying on Friday that the size of additional public works projects must be finalised after looking at various data, such as the government's November monthly economic report.
